tagging_basis: AQA 7037 specification codes; AS units mapped to the matching A-level leaf

units.summary: Explain how one transnational corporation has contributed to globalisation of the world economy.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation needing a named TNC and flows of goods, capital or technology.

units.summary: Analyse temperature and precipitation tables for three Antarctic stations to describe climate characteristics.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of climatic statistics across three sites with latitude and altitude contrast.

units.summary: Assess whether using Antarctica as a global common can ever be sustainable in a globalising world.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay linking threats, management and interdependence; sustained evaluative judgement across the theme.

units.summary: Explain the meanings of endogenous and exogenous factors in the context of place.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of two defined terms; familiar content.

units.summary: Evaluate the usefulness of a 1935 painting and a 2015 photograph for showing economic or demographic and cultural change.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 evaluation of two qualitative visual sources captured at different dates.

units.summary: Assess the usefulness of house price data compared with other quantitative sources for understanding a local place.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1/AO2 evaluation of quantitative source use with an unfamiliar data table and own fieldwork comparison.

units.summary: Assess how far conflict arises when residents resist changes imposed by external agents, using studied places.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay needing place studies, categorised external factors and varied community responses.

units.summary: Outline characteristics of an area undergoing urban resurgence.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a defined process; familiar content.

units.summary: Analyse changes in the world pattern of urbanisation shown in two figures.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of global trends over time from quantitative figures.

units.summary: Assess the extent to which counter-urbanisation leads to social and economic change.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extent item (AO1 4 AO2 5) linking a process to its consequences.

units.summary: Assess whether socio-economic issues matter more than environmental challenges in managing urban areas.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay weighing two issue groups and their management across urban settings.

units.summary: Outline reasons why soil salinisation occurs.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a soil process; more than one reason needed for full marks.

units.summary: Analyse the changes shown in population pyramids for Iran.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of pyramids showing change in age and sex structure over time.

units.summary: Using a map of asylum seeker origins, assess factors accounting for the spatial variation shown.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess item (AO1 4 AO2 5) applying migration knowledge to a novel flow map.

units.summary: Assess the importance of improved health and food security in explaining changing fertility rates.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess item combining vital rates with health and food security and weighing factors.

units.summary: Assess whether current strategies for controlling infectious disease are effective and must change with environmental change.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay requiring disease management knowledge plus future environmental change evaluation.

units.summary: Explain the concept of resource peak.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of a single named concept.

units.summary: Analyse the relationship between GNI per capita and energy consumption per capita from two maps.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of paired choropleth maps and correlation.

units.summary: Using a trend graph, assess the success of strategies to increase supply through nuclear and renewable energy.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess item applying energy mix knowledge to a novel time series.

units.summary: Assess whether conflict over water is inevitable given the widening gap between supply and demand.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extent item evaluating a predicted outcome using water security knowledge.

units.summary: Assess whether physical factors outweigh human factors in managing water supply, now and in future.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay evaluating two factor groups over time with sustained argument.
